newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Sceptical Dutch want EMU referendum -- survey.
newsitem.headline: Sceptical Dutch want EMU referendum -- survey.

text.p: Dutch voters are sceptical about the benefits of European economic and monetary union and want a referendum before they swap their guilders for a single European currency, an opinion poll showed on Wednesday.
The survey, commissioned by Dutch daily NRC Handelsblad, polled 1,200 people across the Netherlands, which currently holds the EU presidency.
One in three polled thought the Netherlands would be worse off under EMU in 20 years' time, while just 12 percent believed the nation stood to benefit.
Another 29 percent of respondents said EMU participation would make no difference one way or another.
More than half those polled (56 percent) said they favoured a referendum on whether the Netherlands should join the single currency bloc, due to be decided in early 1998.
The poll indicated that if a referendum were held now, the Dutch could decide against joining EMU.
NRC Handelsblad said 36 percent would vote against EMU membership while 34 percent would vote in favour.
"The division between those in favour and those against crosses all party lines," the paper said.
The Netherlands is widely tipped to be among the core qualifiers for EMU as it already qualifies on two of the three official entry targets.
But the poll shows Dutch citizens are becoming increasingly doubtful about the euro, the planned pan-European currency.
A quarter of those polled said they had become more opposed to the euro in recent months, while five percent said they had become more enthusiastic, NRC Handelsblad said.

It said that its poll had been based on similar questions to those asked by Gallup in a recent survey commissioned by other European newspapers which showed the French and Italians to be keen proponents of the Euro while Germans were sceptical.
The guilder is one of the strongest currencies in the EU bloc and the Dutch economy is widely seen as something of a model for a post-EMU Europe.
